newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli PM says bombing evidence points to Hamas.
newsitem.headline: Israeli PM says bombing evidence points to Hamas.

text.p: Israel has growing indications that the radical Islamic movement Hamas carried out last month's double suicide bombing in Jerusalem, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday.

He said there was no evidence of involvement by Lebanon's Hizbollah, rejecting assertions by Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat that senior Israeli officers had linked the pro-Iranian group to the attack.
"We have a growing indication of the culpability of (the) Hamas organisation," Netanyahu told U.S. Fox television.
"It's too early to say that definitively but from the preparations, from the statements of taking responsibility, from other intelligence that we have, it points to Hamas," he said.
"We have no indications that it's Hizbollah. Again we cannot say definitively who it is but whoever did this had to base himself on a local organisation," Netanyahu said.
Mystery has surrounded the origin and identity of the two bombers, who killed 13 other people when they blew themselves up in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on July 30.
The attack, the bloodiest of its kind in Israel for over a year, was claimed within hours in a statement issued in the name of Hamas's military wing.
Both Israeli and Palestinian officials have questioned the authenticity of the claim, referring to differences in language and style from previous Hamas statements.

Arafat has argued that the bombers probably came from abroad, in a defence against sanctions imposed by Israel on Palestinian areas after the bombing and charges from Netanyahu that he has failed to crack down on Moslem militants.
He noted on Saturday that the claim of responsibility had contained a call for the release by Israel of kidnapped Hizbollah cleric Sheikh Abdel Karim Obeid.
"What is the relation of Hizbollah with this terrorist activity unless they were behind it or they knew it or they facilitated....it?" Arafat asked.
"I am not blaming anybody. I am telling you what had been mentioned by the high Israeli officers," Arafat told Reuters, CNN and Abu Dhabi television in a joint interview.
Hizbollah, which is fighting to drive Israel and its Lebanese militia allies from an Israeli occupation zone in south Lebanon, denounced Arafat on Sunday for spreading "lies".

"Arafat has unleashed a series of false accusations and lies targeting Hizbollah and naming it in the course of a campaign coordinated with the Zionist entity (Israel)," the group said in a statement.

Violence has increased along the Israel-Lebanon border in the past week. Fourteen people, seven of them Lebanese civilians, have been killed in Israeli air raids, artillery shelling or bombs planted by unknown assailants since Monday.
